validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, federally docketed project. MARAD/USCG Docket No. MARAD-2019-0095: West Delta LNG, LLC (a Delaware LLC and subsidiary of LNG 21, LLC, per the applicant's own Summarized Basis of Design) filed a deepwater port license application initially received August 28, 2019 (date per MARAD's Dec 31, 2024 letter); Federal Register Notice of Application 2019-20929 (09/26/2019) and Notice of Intent/public meeting 2019-21567 (10/04/2019, 84 FR 53218) both confirm the docket and reprint the application's 'Summary of the Application'. CLASSIFICATION: correct as an LNG-feed-gas transmission pipeline -- the FR notice describes a proposed 30-inch pipeline running from the onshore Venice Pretreatment Plant (Plaquemines Parish, LA) to the offshore West Delta LNG deepwater port/liquefaction platform (OCS West Delta Lease Block 44, ~10.5 nautical miles off Plaquemines Parish), i.e. a feed-gas line supplying an LNG export terminal, not a gathering or distribution line. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of anything else in this 44-row roster -- 'West Delta LNG' / 'West Delta LNG LLC' / docket MARAD-2019-0095 is a single, standalone deepwater-port project with no other GEM PID referencing the same docket or the Venice Gas Complex feed-gas line. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1/Operator = 'West Delta LNG LLC' (100%) is uncontested and directly confirmed -- the FR notice names 'West Delta LNG LLC (Applicant)' as the party seeking to own, construct, and operate the facility; LNG 21, LLC (Houston) is the parent sponsor entity (per the Basis of Design filing and The Advocate's 'LNG 21, the Houston firm behind the West Delta LNG port'), consistent with, not contradicting, the sheet's Owner1 value. LOCATION: the routes-repo geojson for P3665 has no drawn geometry ({'geometry': null}) -- there is no route-vs-sheet mismatch to adjudicate; StartState/Province=Louisiana / EndState/Province=Louisiana / CountryOrArea=United States are both correct per the FR notice (onshore terminus in Plaquemines Parish, LA; offshore terminus on the Louisiana OCS).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=proposed is stale and wrong; the application was terminated. Evidence chain: MARAD's own Dec 31, 2024 letter (federal primary record) gave LNG 21 an explicit ultimatum -- withdraw voluntarily or be denied -- after seven prior extensions dating to 2019, with a 14-day response deadline of Jan 14, 2025. Earthworks' Dec 9, 2025 press release (independent NGO, a genuinely separate origin from the MARAD letter) confirms the outcome played out: MARAD 'has terminated the deepwater port license application for West Delta LNG', with LNG 21 having received an eighth extension since Dec 2019 and still failing to submit a viable application. This is a confirmed, sourced discrete regulatory event (not a GEM dormancy inference), so ShelvedCancelledType='confirmed' rather than 'inferred', and 'cancelled' (not 'shelved') is the correct terminal state given MARAD affirmatively terminated the docket rather than merely going quiet on it. CancelledYear is set to 2025 (the year Earthworks reports the termination); I could not obtain the single definitive final termination/denial letter itself (regulations.gov document IDs guessed in the MARAD-2019-0095-0039 through -0042 range all returned HTTP 403, which is inconclusive access-blocking rather than evidence the documents don't exist), so no more precise month is asserted for CancelledYear/CancelledMonth beyond what these two verified sources state. Two independent origins meet the corroboration bar: a MARAD federal record and an independent NGO press release, not the same document restated twice. StartYear1 (2023, unsupported -- see the validity spec concern) and Construction/SegmentCost (both blank, left UNRESOLVED) are all consistent with a project that never advanced past pre-EIS scoping before being terminated.
